dataset.modifications: Selected original record 231 samples 0–3599 (0–10 seconds) in both original channels. Decoded WFDB format 212 and converted ADC values to mV using (ADC − 1024) / 200. Serialized as JSON. No filtering, smoothing, normalization, interpolation, resampling, synthetic leads, or waveform replacement was applied. Original beat/comment annotations are included, separately from manually estimated teaching P onsets.
dataset.samplingNote: Original 360 Hz, 10 seconds, two ambulatory channels: MLII and V1.
dataset.annotationNote: QRS anchors are exact event sample positions from the original 231.atr file. The 11 P-wave onsets are approximate visual estimates for animation only, not source-validated fiducial measurements. QRS onset, QRS duration, electrical propagation and all mechanical motion in the 3D model remain teaching approximations.
dataset.coverageNote: The source explicitly identifies Mobitz II in the opening strip. Coexisting rate-related RBBB is preserved. Only actual source channels are provided.

records.title: Mobitz II AV block · RBBB
records.description: An authentic ambulatory ECG from MIT-BIH record 231. The source explicitly identifies Mobitz II block in the opening strip. A visible P wave near 5.76 seconds is not followed by a QRS; compare the conducted beats before and after it. The source also identifies rate-related right bundle branch block. Only the two recorded channels, MLII and V1, are available.
records.attribution: Contains information from the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database v1.0.0, by George Moody and Roger Mark, made available by PhysioNet under the Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0 (ODC-By). DOI: 10.13026/C2F305.
records.leadConfigurationNote: MLII is a modified limb lead II recorded with chest electrodes. Its 3D lead axis is omitted because the source does not supply the exact modified electrode geometry. V1 is the source label for the second ambulatory chest channel and remains available for comparison. This is not a standard simultaneous 12-lead ECG; no missing leads are reconstructed.

sourceLabels.description: Mobitz II AV block in the opening example, with rate-related right bundle branch block

sourceLabels.scope: All 10 annotated QRS events in the selected excerpt

sourceLabels.description: Normal sinus rhythm annotation at the start of the source record; the intermittent Mobitz II event is identified by the source narrative and missed-beat comment

records.labelExplanation: The Mobitz II subtype comes from the original record narrative and the official directory description of the opening strip. It is not inferred from a 2:1 conduction pattern. Beat labels and comments retain the source terminology. Recording labels are not independently re-adjudicated by this website.
records.sourceValidationNote: MIT-BIH reference annotations were reviewed by two cardiologists, with disagreements resolved by consensus. The additional P-onset estimates in this export have not undergone that source annotation process.

sourceSignalQuality.directoryAssessment: Both channels clean throughout the source record
sourceSignalQuality.processing: Original baseline variation and noise preserved

coexistingFindings: Source documents rate-related right bundle branch block; all 10 QRS events in this excerpt carry the original R label.
The wider source record also contains 2:1 AV-block periods and ectopic events. Those later sections are not included in this opening excerpt.
records.subtypeEvidence: The original 231.hea explicitly mentions Mobitz II. The official MIT-BIH directory labels its 0:02 sample strip as sinus rhythm with Mobitz II and RBBB. This first-ten-second export contains the isolated missed-beat comment at sample 2083 and the visible nonconducted P in the corresponding pause.
notes: Authentic deidentified clinical recording, with the original source diagnostic context retained.
360 Hz original samples: approximately 2.78 ms per sample. No additional signal processing was applied.
This source has two ambulatory channels, MLII and V1. It does not contain the other ten standard ECG leads.
A source MISSB comment occurs at 5.786 seconds. That comment is not a validated P-onset annotation; the visible P onset is estimated separately for animation.
Source beat labels indicate RBBB; its rate-related morphology can vary. The reference heart does not reconstruct every beat-specific conduction detail.

QRS anchors are exact event sample positions from the original 231.atr file. The 11 P-wave onsets are approximate visual estimates for animation only, not source-validated fiducial measurements. QRS onset, QRS duration, electrical propagation and all mechanical motion in the 3D model remain teaching approximations.

profile.title: Mobitz II AV block · RBBB
profile.summary: A recorded nonconducted P wave interrupts successive conducted beats, with coexisting rate-related RBBB.
profile.electrical: The original source identifies Mobitz II AV block. Atrial activity continues through the missing ventricular event near 5.76 seconds. The reference activation model also illustrates the source-documented RBBB; it is not a reconstruction of this patient’s conduction system.
profile.mechanical: Approximate P onsets drive the atrial animation and original beat markers anchor ventricular events. The blocked atrial event has no corresponding ventricular contraction. Regional contraction strength, exact conduction delay and all cardiac motion are illustrative.
profile.observe: Use MLII to follow the P wave near 5.76 seconds that has no QRS after it. Compare conducted PR intervals on either side of that pause; use the original trace rather than the approximate animation anchors. V1 shows the coexisting, rate-dependent bundle-branch morphology.

notes: The QRS event positions come from the original 231.atr annotations, typically aligned to a major QRS extremum. They are not QRS-onset measurements.
P-wave starts are approximate manual estimates with uncertainty of several tens of milliseconds, for synchronization only. Do not report clinical PR measurements from these anchors.
A 45 ms offset from each source beat marker estimates QRS onset; a 140 ms reference duration illustrates RBBB. Neither is a source fiducial measurement, and actual morphology varies.
The nonconducted P estimate at 5.735 seconds corresponds to the visible atrial deflection and the source MISSB comment at 5.786 seconds. No synthetic beat is inserted into the ECG.
teaching.mechanismModelNote: The anatomical and activation animation is a schematic teaching model; it is not patient-specific motion or measured tissue activation.
